suggestedSeverity.reasoning: A real assurance weakness that can convert an unexpected detail-free refusal into a silent pass, and it must be fixed before promotion. It is not MUST-severity as a defect of the SUBJECT, because no currently-masked failure exists: running the proposed checker over the unchanged frozen corpus yields an identical 1787/1787 with an identical (empty) failure set, so no verdict in the canonical run changes. Root may elevate on promotion-gate grounds; I record the evidential basis rather than the label.

theDefect.mechanism: In each handler the EXPECTATION side is a defaulting `.get`, so a case that expects success (no `refusal` key) yields None; a refusal raised with `detail is None` then satisfies `None == None` and the check PASSES although an unexpected refusal occurred.
theDefect.reachability: Detail-free refusals are real and reachable - for example repair_preview raises Refusal('REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED', None, 'target fingerprint not in the evidence Run', t) and admit_evidence_requirement raises Refusal(CONFIG.INVALID, None, ...).
theDefect.whyTheGuardIsTheCheckersOwnLaw: Each of these handlers is already paired with a post-try `if 'refusal' in exp: check(cid, False, 'no refusal')` for the opposite direction. The checker therefore ALREADY uses key membership to mean "a refusal was expected"; the proposal restores that same convention to the raised-refusal direction. It is a restoration of the existing meaning, not a new law.

scopeCompleteness.method: I derived the defect signature independently and scanned the whole checker with it: a comparison is false-pass-capable only when the EXPECTATION side is a defaulting .get AND the comparison is control-flow-selected by a raised exception.
scopeCompleteness.theOtherFifteen: Not equivalent. In every one the `.get` is on the OBSERVED side and the expectation is INDEXED (exp[...]), so an absent expectation raises KeyError and fails loudly rather than passing silently.
scopeCompleteness.theOneNearMiss: Line 146 is the only expectation-side `.get` outside a handler: t.get('errorCode') == g.get('errorCode') in the D9 GOLDEN comparison, where both sides default and absence-matching-absence is the intended semantics (the neighbouring `(t.get('reasonCodes') or [None])[0]` idiom normalises absence deliberately). Correctly left alone; guarding it would break a golden that declares no error code.
scopeCompleteness.conclusion: Ten is the complete set for this checker. I found no missed equivalent.
